- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 90+ → 92+), then sharply correct downward.
- Mean reversion is strong in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; model fails to reflect this, often holding high values.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; underestimates downward trends until 3–5 days later.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 3–5 days, especially when history shows recent volatility or downward momentum.
- Model tends to ignore recent low prices in the 30-day history when forecasting, leading to persistent overestimation.
- When true outcome is below 85, model often fails to adjust downward quickly, especially if recent history includes low values.
- Forecasts are sensitive to recent high values; if last 5–7 days are above 90, model often overreacts with high forecasts.
- Model underestimates downward momentum when true outcome shows rapid decline after a spike.
- Forecasts are too smooth; fail to capture short-term volatility or sudden reversals in the last 5–10 days.
